col4_Comment: DSNY predicts that this figure is much larger than this, but data collection constraints exist in the data in the commercial and construction & demolition waste industries. This figure represents residential waste including government operations. Curbside and Containerized collection routes serve individual districts; trucks on these routes pass over scales each day which transmit tonnage data into DSNY's centralized computer system. For this reason, monthly statistics, by Community Districts, can be tracked and reported. Additional tonnage managed by DSNY (in commercial, construction & demolition, to name a few areas) is diverted through other mechanisms and transfer facilities but is only available on a voluntary reporting basis. Materials including Textile & Used Materials Donations, E-Waste, Hazardous Waste, other Organics collections, Redeemed Bottle & Can Deposit containers, and other take-back and diversion programs are included on the annual report from DSNY only and contribute to an overall annual diversion percentage of DSNY-managed waste that is different from the real total.

La disposición de los residuos sólidos urbanos se realiza en las celdas ubicadas dentro de las zonas licenciadas del Parque de Innovación Doña Juana (PIDJ). Estos residuos se depositan en las terrazas de acuerdo con lo estipulado en el Contrato de Concesión 344 de 2010, suscrito con el concesionario CGR.
Actualmente, no existe un aprovechamiento directo de los residuos como recurso energético; este se realiza indirectamente a través de los subproductos generados por su descomposición en las celdas. Es importante destacar que, durante el proceso de degradación de los residuos sólidos urbanos, se generan subproductos como lixiviados, biogás y una fracción residual de biomasa que permanece en las terrazas de disposición.
El biogás generado en un relleno sanitario es una mezcla de gases que se forma como resultado de diversos factores físicos, químicos y procesos microbiológicos que ocurren dentro de la masa
de residuos, afectando especialmente la fracción
orgánica de estos. Es importante destacar que
los residuos que ingresan diariamente al Relleno
Sanitario Doña Juana (RSDJ) presentan una composición variable y en constante cambio.
Mediante el aprovechamiento del biogás se realiza la generación de energía mediante cuatro (4) moto generadores, los cuales hacen parte de la etapa de ampliación de la plataforma de aprovechamiento Doña Juana I, con lo cual se completó una capacidad instalada de 5,3MW. Por lo anterior, no se tiene un estimativo preciso de la cantidad de residuos que se utilizan para la generación de energía, ya que la generación no se realiza con tecnología de termovalorización, sino utilizando el biogás proveniente de las celdas de disposición para la combustión en motores acoplados a generadores.

The electricity produced from incineration is used to operate the plant, with the surplus being sold to ERDF. col4_Comment: A human error was corrected from 2022 which was short of 100 000 ML.\n\nSUPPLYING THE CAPITAL WITH WATER WHERE DOES PARIS' WATER COME FROM? A Diverse Supply: The production and distribution methods of water in Paris have been inherited from the late 19th century, a time when underground water sources were favored. Half of the capital's potable water supply still comes from these sources. Surface waters from the Seine and Marne rivers complement the production and distribution system to meet all needs. The underground waters are extracted from 102 wells, located 70 to 150 kilometers from the capital, near the cities of Sens, Provins, and Fontainebleau in the southeast, and Dreux and Verneuil-sur-Avre in the west. They are transported by three main aqueducts: the Avre aqueduct to the west, and the Vanne and Loing aqueducts to the south. These waters are treated either at the source or upon their arrival in Paris. Surface waters taken from the Seine and Marne rivers are treated at the Orly and Joinville plants, respectively. The waters are then chlorinated to ensure their bacteriological quality during their transport to Parisian reservoirs and then to consumption points. EVOLUTION OF WATER VOLUMES PRODUCED, EXCHANGED, USED BY THE SERVICE, AND DELIVERED TO PARIS BETWEEN 2019 AND 2022 (expressed in thousands of cubic meters): The maximum production capacity of Eau de Paris is one million cubic meters per day: 400,000 m³/day of underground waters: Voulzie springs: 50,000 m³/day; Waters drawn from the Vals de Seine catchment area: 50,000 m³/day; Springs of the Loing and Lunain valleys: 50,000 m³/day; Springs of the Vanne valley and Saint Ange stream: 150,000 m³/day; Springs and catchment areas of the Avre and Eure valleys: 100,000 m³/day.

row_name: Percentage of wastewater safely treated to at least secondary level (%)
col4_Comment: A UNIQUE SEWER NETWORK This network serves three essential functions: The collection of wastewater and stormwater within Paris and their transportation to the main outfall sewer, which are large-diameter pipes that ensure their evacuation to interdepartmental treatment plants; The transportation of effluents from upstream departments (Val-de-Marne, Seine-Saint-Denis) to these same outfall sewers; It also functions as a technical gallery due to its accessible design, housing potable and non-potable water pipes, and in certain areas, chilled water pipes for air conditioning, low-voltage cables, and fiber optics. In the new ZAC Batignolles district, it even includes pipes for pneumatic waste collection. The Parisian sanitation network is almost entirely of the \'combined\' type, meaning it collects both domestic and industrial wastewater and rainwater in the same system. The average daily flow of combined effluents (wastewater and stormwater) transported by the Parisian sanitation network in 2022 was approximately 841,335 m³/day, including 634,478 m³/day of wastewater discharged by Parisians and municipal services using non-potable water. COLLECTING WATER, VALORIZING INFRASTRUCTURE AND EFFLUENTS, DIVERSIFYING THE NETWORK'S USES The network has some specific features: Its operation is largely gravity-fed. However, five pumping stations continuously lift water from the low-lying 12th and 13th districts; It is almost entirely composed of accessible structures, totaling 2,500 km in length, including around 143 km of main outfall sewers and large collectors, and 730 km of ancillary structures (private connections, storm drains, inspection chamber connections); The dimensions of the structures and the existence of 39 storm overflows that discharge excess water directly into the Seine help prevent overloading and overflow of the network during heavy rains. A central \'control and command\' station connected to 140 local management stations in the sewer network (plants, storm overflows, grids, measurement sites) allows real-time monitoring and action on pumps and valves, enabling optimized flow management. It also provides the necessary elements to produce a monthly self-monitoring report of the network, which helps track events (rainfall, etc.) and assess the proper functioning of the equipment.60% of the treated sludge is directly utilized for agricultural purposes

question_text: Report the following waste-related data for your jurisdiction.
row_name: Total amount of solid waste generated (tonnes/year)
col4_Comment: The annual solid waste amount for Ankara was estimated at approximately 1.36 million tonnes for 2025. This figure was calculated by extrapolating eight months of 2025 municipal waste collection records to a full year. Data originates from the Ankara Metropolitan Municipality (AMM), which oversees solid waste management across all districts, with contractors carrying out operational collection. Household billing records and district-level collection logs were used to verify the accuracy of daily volumes. The scope includes residential, commercial, institutional, and bulky waste managed as municipal solid waste. Construction and demolition waste, as well as hazardous industrial waste, are excluded. This methodology aligns with the Global Covenant of Mayors (GCoM) reporting requirements and ensures jurisdiction-level accuracy.

question_text: Report the following waste-related data for your jurisdiction.
row_name: Percentage of the total solid waste generated that is utilized for waste to energy (%)
col4_Comment: Approximately 12% of Ankara's municipal solid waste is currently utilized for waste-to-energy processes. This includes incineration with energy recovery and the capture of biogas from landfills. The figure is derived from the AMM's Greenhouse Gas Inventory (YIDEP, 2019) updated with International Training Center (ITC) waste characterization tables. Waste-to-energy facilities remain limited in scale, but pilot anaerobic digestion units treating organic waste are operational and expanding. Energy recovery contributes to both electricity and heat generation, supporting climate mitigation goals. However, most waste continues to be disposed of in landfills, highlighting the need for increased investment in circular economy infrastructure.

question_text: Report the following waste-related data for your jurisdiction.
row_name: Percentage of the total solid waste generated that is diverted away from landfill and incineration (%)
col4_Comment: Diversion of solid waste away from landfill and incineration is reported at 28%. This indicator covers materials recovered for recycling, composting, or direct reuse. Data is compiled from the AMM's Circular Economy Unit and validated using ITC composition analyses. The increase in diversion compared to previous years reflects new separation-at-source initiatives introduced in selected neighborhoods, educational institutions, and commercial sectors. Although progress has been made, diversion levels remain below EU averages, suggesting a strong potential for scaling up circular economy practices.

question_text: Report the following waste-related data for your jurisdiction.
row_name: Percentage of the diverted solid waste generated that is recycled (%)
col4_Comment: Out of the total diverted waste streams, 21% is recycled through formal systems. Recycled materials include paper, cardboard, plastics, metals, glass, and compostable green waste. The data is based on AMM contractor reports and ITC waste composition surveys. Informal recycling activities exist in Ankara but are not fully integrated into municipal reporting. These activities contribute additional recycling volumes, meaning the actual figure could be slightly higher. Recycling rates are expected to improve as source separation programs expand and new recycling infrastructure is commissioned.

question_text: Report the following waste-related data for your jurisdiction.
row_name: Percentage of the diverted solid waste generated that is reused (%)
col4_Comment: Around 7% of the diverted waste stream is reused, primarily through the recovery of bulky waste such as furniture, appliances, and construction materials. The Ankara Metropolitan Municipality supports reuse through dedicated collection programs and partnerships with second-hand markets. Data is derived from AMM reuse initiatives and ITC methodologies. While reuse remains a smaller component of waste diversion, it contributes to resource efficiency and reduces demand for raw materials. Expansion of reuse centers and public awareness campaigns are planned to enhance this share in future reporting cycles.

question_text: Report the following waste-related data for your jurisdiction.
row_name: Percentage of waste collected where separation at source is taking place (%)
col4_Comment: Source separation currently accounts for 15% of total waste collected in Ankara. Programs are concentrated in pilot neighborhoods, commercial facilities, and schools, where households and businesses separate recyclable materials before collection. Participation rates are tracked through surveys and verified by contractors. While the current percentage remains limited, AMM plans to expand separation-at-source coverage citywide to meet EU waste targets and GCoM commitments. Household engagement and infrastructure investments will be crucial for achieving higher participation rates.

question_text: Report the following waste-related data for your jurisdiction.
row_name: Total annual amount of food waste produced in the jurisdiction (tonnes/year)
col4_Comment: Food waste in Ankara is estimated at around 280,000 tonnes annually, representing approximately 20% of total municipal solid waste. This estimate is derived from ITC waste characterization tables and applied to the 2025 total waste amount. Food waste originates from households, restaurants, and commercial food supply chains. Pilot projects for food waste prevention and composting are underway but remain small in scale. The magnitude of food waste highlights the need for stronger prevention programs, redistribution systems, and organic waste valorization.

Information provided by Msunduzi Municipalities Waste Management Unit 




IDP 22/27-pg 193: SOLID WASTE MANAGEMENT There are two components to solid waste in the Municipality, namely Solid Waste Removal and Solid Waste Disposal.1. SOLID WASTE REMOVALIn terms of the Census (2011) information, weekly refuse removal has declined from 59.5% in 2001 to 53.2% in 2011, but this could be associated with a growth in the number of households. Of the approximately 94 000 households in the 'borough' of Pietermaritzburg, approximately 84 000 are receiving weekly refuse removal. The Solid Waste Removal section in the Municipality is responsible for the following areas:• Waste Collection;• Management of Garden Sites (Prestbury, Link Road, Grange, Richie Road, Sobantu, South Road, Woodlands, and Eastwood);• Street Sweeping;• Maintenance of Public Convenience (toilets); and• Eradication of Illegal Dumping.2. SOLID WASTE DISPOSALThe New England Road Landfill Site is a licensed facility that is managed by the Municipality, and is the largest disposal facility in the KZN Midlands. The Site spans an area of 44 hectares, of which 29 hectares is currently being filled. The Site is managed in terms of its permit requirements, and in terms of relevant environmental legislation.The Landfill is classified as a general, large, leachate bearing site, and does not accept any hazardous waste. The Site is equipped with two weighbridges and a billing system, and users of the site are billed for the disposal of waste as per Council's tariff of charges. Waste disposed of is captured on the waste information system percategory and type of waste. It is a regional facility that accepts waste from some of the local municipalities under the jurisdiction of the uMgungundlovu District. Quarterly monitoring for gas emissions, groundwater and surfacewater contamination, and leachate disposal is conducted to ensure that the surrounding environment, water courses, and groundwater are not being contaminated.The site currently has a lifespan of seven years, and feasibility studies into implementing advanced waste management systems aimed at reducing waste to landfill are being considered to extend the lifespan. Some of these initiatives involve recycling at source, implementation of a waste recycling collection system, the construction of a Materials Recovery Facility, and the construction an organic waste composting facility to treat organic waste.

col4_Comment:
El dato de residuos municipales generados se corresponde con el año 2022. En general, Vitoria-Gasteiz mantiene niveles de generación de años anteriores, aunque en esta
ocasión se produce una importante bajada en la generación de residuos mezclados. Este hecho,
acompañado del fuerte incremento en algunas recogidas selectivas, ha permitido mejorar la
calidad de la recogida de residuos, alcanzando su máximo histórico en recogida selectiva global. El 38% de ellos se recogen selectivamente en origen (la recogida mayoritaria sigue siendo la de residuos mezclados, sin embargo, las recogidas
selectivas han aumentado varios puntos respecto al anterior ejercicio). Este incremento de las
selectivas se puede asociar prácticamente por entero a la recogida de biorresiduos, que pasan
de un cuarto puesto entre las selectivas a una segunda posición, a poca distancia del papel y
cartón recogidos selectivamente. Por primera vez la eliminación como tratamiento finalista cae por
debajo del 50% y se acompaña de un incremento notable en el valor de reciclaje, alcanzando el
valor más alto de toda la serie de datos. El resto son tratados en una planta de tratamiento mecánico-biológico, en la que se recupera un 5% adicional de materiales a reciclaje, se obtiene biogás, que se utiliza para producir energía eléctrica (125% sobre el consumo eléctrico de la planta), y se obtiene un biorresiduo estabilizado, que se elimina finalmente en vertedero. Los servicios de recogida y tratamiento de residuos se llevan a cabo por el ayuntamiento a través de una contrata. El documento anexado recoge datos relativos a los residuos municipales del conjunto del territorio de Álava, cuya capital es Vitoria. Los datos correspondientes a Vitoria-Gasteiz están en el apartado 2.7.
https://web.araba.eus/documents/1247685/1248563/01+Inventario+de+residuos+Araba+2022.pdf/9a94b71d-4396-33e7-0558-a2ad0a9dfdd3?t=1696313527136
En 2022, se hizo un cálculo de la Huella de Carbono, alcances 1, 2 3 de la recogida y gestión de Residuos Domésticos, según metodología GHG Protocol, resultando ser, para Vitoria-Gasteiz, de 38.935,40 t CO2 e y 0,407 t CO2 e/t residuo, 1.970,05 t CO2 por el transporte de sus residuos, 1.043,45 t CO2, por la clasificación y 35.808,12 t CO2 por tratamiento. El método de cálculo para el año 2022, se replica
para los años anteriores de 2021, 2020 y 2019, y da una disminución en las emisiones debidas a residuos de 2.000 tn CO2 e en 3 años.

Si bien la municipalidad ha implementado diferentes mecanismos para el almacenamiento y recolección de los residuos ya sea en la

Solid waste is diverted away from the landfill and incineration in the following programs: Mixed Recycling, Glass Recycling, 50% of Hefty Renew Orange Bag Program materials diverted to mechanical recycling end-markets, Residential Compost, 95% of HHW, 95% of Commercial Hazardous Waste, Commercial Wood Recycling, and Deconstruction & Demolition Recycling.

Solid waste is NOT diverted away from the landfill and incineration in the following programs: Trash, 50% of Hefty Renew Orange Bag Program materials diverted to waste to energy programs, 5% of HHW landfilled or treated and disposed, 5% of Commercial Hazardous Waste landfilled or treated and disposed, and Medication Waste incinerated.'

Finally, the City of Boise has a Deconstruction and Demolition ordinance which requires contractors to work to salvage, recycle, and reuse materials through local recycling companies who are notified at permit application. col4_Comment:
Tingkat daur ulang sampah di Kota Medan tahun 2024 hanya mencapai 14,80% dari total timbulan sampah. Dengan volume timbulan sampah tahun 2024 sebesar 632.149,41 ton, hanya sekitar 93.557 ton yang didaur ulang (14,80%). Angka ini menunjukkan tantangan besar dalam pengelolaan sampah berkelanjutan karena mayoritas sampah masih belum dimanfaatkan dan akhirnya berakhir di TPA (Tempat Pemrosesan Akhir), khususnya TPA Terjun.

Faktor Penyebab Rendahnya Tingkat Daur Ulang
a. Rendahnya Pemilahan Sampah dari Sumber
Mayoritas rumah tangga tidak memisahkan sampah organik dan anorganik. Berdasarkan data SIPSN, komposisi sampah di Medan didominasi oleh:
- Sampah organik (sisa makanan) 40%.
- Sampah plastik 15%.
Tanpa pemilahan, sampah yang seharusnya dapat didaur ulang bercampur dengan sampah organik sehingga sulit diolah.
b. Infrastruktur Daur Ulang yang Terbatas
TPST (Tempat Pengolahan Sampah Terpadu) dan bank sampah belum mencukupi untuk menampung dan mengolah volume sampah yang besar. Sistem pengangkutan sampah masih berfokus pada pengumpulan dan pembuangan, bukan pemrosesan atau pemanfaatan.
c. Minimnya Edukasi dan Partisipasi Masyarakat
Kesadaran masyarakat untuk memilah sampah masih rendah. Program 3R (Reduce, Reuse, Recycle) belum berjalan optimal.
d. Penggunaan Plastik Sekali Pakai yang Tinggi
Sampah plastik dari produk kemasan mencapai 15% dari total sampah. Plastik sekali pakai sulit terurai, sehingga menambah beban pengolahan dan mencemari lingkungan jika tidak didaur ulang.

question_text: Report the following waste-related data for your jurisdiction.
row_name: Total amount of solid waste generated (tonnes/year)
col4_Comment: O município de Santo André destaca-se por sua gestão técnica e sustentável de resíduos sólidos, coordenada pelo Departamento de Resíduos Sólidos do SEMASA (Serviço Municipal de Saneamento Ambiental de Santo André), responsável por toda a cadeia de gestão de resíduos no município. O serviço de coleta é realizado por meio de contratação de empresa terceirizada, com supervisão direta do SEMASA, garantindo conformidade com as diretrizes municipais e nacionais. Com base em dados internos do Departamento de Resíduos Sólidos, os números referem-se especificamente aos resíduos coletados pelo SEMASA, que totalizaram 239.054,60 toneladas no último ano. Este volume compreende resíduos úmidos, secos e de serviços de saúde, coletados em todo o município. Um dos pilares dessa gestão é a realização periódica de estudos gravimétricos, que permitem um diagnóstico preciso e quantificado dos resíduos coletados. Por meio desses estudos, é possível caracterizar detalhadamente a composição dos resíduos, identificando as porcentagens de materiais recicláveis, orgânicos, rejeitos e outros componentes. Este levantamento quantitativo, aliado à análise gravimétrica, é fundamental para: dimensionar e otimizar os serviços de coleta e transporte; avaliar a efetividade de programas de reciclagem e compostagem; identificar oportunidades para a redução de produção de resíduos na fonte; planejar a expansão ou a adaptação da infraestrutura de tratamento e destinação. Além disso, o monitoramento constante permite que o município acompanhe a evolução dos indicadores ao longo do tempo. Conforme os dados internos do Departamento: 0% dos resíduos sólidos coletados são utilizados para transformação em energia; 1,66% do total de resíduos coletados não é enviado para aterros ou incineração, representando o volume efetivamente desviado (ou seja, é a quantidade que é desviada da disposição final ou incineração de um total que considera úmidos, secos e serviços de saúde); 100% dos materiais que chegam às cooperativas são triados e reciclados, sendo que os rejeitos deste processo seguem para disposição final. Dessa forma, Santo André consolida um modelo de gestão de resíduos alinhado com a Política Nacional de Resíduos Sólidos, reforçando seu compromisso com a sustentabilidade e a qualidade de vida da população.

question_text: Report the following waste-related data for your jurisdiction.
row_name: Volume of wastewater produced within the jurisdiction boundary (megalitres/year)
col1_Data availability: Reporting state/regional data scaled to jurisdiction-level
col4_Comment:
Our population is approximately 358,954 (2021 Census). Sydney Water reports an average daily water consumption of 160 liters per person in their service area. Assuming 80% of water consumed becomes wastewater, this = to 128 liters per person per day.

Daily wastewater generation: 358,954 people * 128 L/person = 45,946,112 liters
Annual wastewater generation: 45,946,112 L/day * 365 days/year = 16,772,240,680 liters
Conversion to megaliters: 16,772,240,680 liters / 1,000,000 L/ML = approximately 16,772 megaliters/year

col4_Comment: La population de la ville d'Abidjan s'est considérablement accrue ces dernières années. Cette croissance s'est accompagnée d'une forte urbanisation et d'une croissance industrielle non contrôlées. A cela s'ajoute une absence de structure de surveillance efficace et surtout un non respect de la réglementation environnementale. La production importante de déchets domestiques, industriels et hospitaliers qui en résulte, est confrontée à une gestion insuffisante et à des problèmes d'infrastructures et de difficultés économiques. Les quantités de déchets générés en 2002, par la ville sont estimées à 1 225 688,97 tonnes (soit 0,98 kg/ha/jour) contre 193 186 m3/j de volume d'eaux usées domestiques. Le réseau d'assainissement présente un faible taux de couverture de la population (29%) en raison du dysfonctionnement de la quasi-totalité des ouvrages existant. Cette situation entraîne un rejet journalier dans la nature, hors des systèmes d'égout, de plus de 115 912 m3 soit 60% des eaux usées avec une charge polluante correspondante estimée à plus de 56 113 kg de DBO5. A cela s'ajoute l'accumulation, chaque année, de près de 550 000 tonnes de déchets ménagers non ramassés et dont les corollaires sont l'engorgement permanent de toutes les communes d'une quantité importante de déchets ménagers et partant des difficultés d'écoulement des eaux usées et pluviales.

col4_Comment: As an upper-tier municipal government, Durham Region provides programs and services to over 215,000 households within eight municipalities: Ajax, Brock, Clarington, Oshawa, Pickering, Scugog, Uxbridge and Whitby. The Region continues to deliver innovative waste reduction, diversion, and disposal programs to meet the needs of the growing population. Collection: Durham Region manages curbside collection of recyclables, organics, leaf and yard waste and residual garbage in Ajax, Brock, Clarington, Pickering, Scugog and Uxbridge. The Region collects recycling in Whitby and Oshawa, but partners with both municipalities to ensure uniform collection programs Region-wide. Bulky, metal goods, waste electrical and electronic equipment, battery, and porcelain collection is also provided to single family homes in Ajax, Brock, Clarington, Pickering, Scugog and Uxbridge by the Region. In addition to curbside collection services, over 400 multi-residential buildings and townhouses are also serviced by the Region of Durham's weekly waste collection programs. Onsite collection services offered in the buildings include recyclables, battery and e-waste collection. Durham Region manages disposal of residual waste from all eight of its local area municipalities. Disposal: Within the Region's 5R hierarchy (Rethink, Reduce, Reuse, Recycle, Recover), the preferred final disposal destination is energy-from-waste at the Durham York Energy Centre (DYEC) in Clarington to maximize the benefit of capturing energy from residual waste. The energy-from-waste process reduces the volume of residential waste by approximately 85to 90 per cent. The largest portion of the waste remaining after processing is, non-hazardous bottom ash. The smaller portion is fly ash with lime and carbon residue from onsite treatment which is captured in the air pollution control equipment. Ash at the DYEC is tested to ensure that it is non-hazardous before being shipped offsite. Bottom ash and treated fly ash are transported to landfill and used as daily cover material, reducing the need for soil or other cover materials. In the year 2023, the total garbage collected and processed by DYEC was 140,000 tonnes. The same year, Durham Region residents generated 33,510 tonnes of source separated organics from the Green Bin program which represents 17.4 per cent of the Region's overall diversion achievement via processing organic waste into compost.

Solid waste collection services in the City of Butuan are undertaken by the City Government through the City Environment and Natural Resources Department (CENRD). The City's solid waste management system is designed to begin at the point of generation, households, commercial establishments, and institutions, where wastes are required to be properly segregated prior to collection. Collection at this level is carried out by the respective barangays, following their prescribed schedules.

Collected and segregated wastes are temporarily stored at the Barangay Materials Recovery Facilities (MRFs). Subsequently, the CENRD retrieves the wastes from the barangay MRFs and transports them to the City Sanitary Landfill Facility (SLF) for appropriate disposal.

It is noteworthy that, prior to 2024, CENRD collection services were limited to 51 out of 86 barangays in the city. Commencing in May 2024, the Department expanded its operations to cover all 86 barangays, thereby ensuring full city-wide service coverage.

Furthermore, since 2024, the strict enforcement of the “No Segregation, No Collection” policy has been implemented in accordance with Republic Act No. 9003, otherwise known as the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000. In compliance with this law, the management of biodegradable and recyclable wastes is devolved to the barangays, while the City Government, through the CENRD, assumes responsibility for the collection and disposal of residual and special wastes.

The current status of Solid Waste Management (SWM) in Quảng Bình province shows certain progress, but the locality still faces many challenges regarding infrastructure and treatment technology.
1. Solid Waste Generation Status
•	Total Generation: Quảng Bình generates an estimated over 600 tons of Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) daily. Although it is a Central region province with a relatively small population, the rapid pace of socio-economic development, especially tourism, has led to an increase in waste volume.
•	Source Separation: Currently, waste source separation activities are not implemented uniformly or widely, which complicates collection and treatment processes and reduces recycling efficiency.
2. Waste Management and Treatment
•	Collection Rate: The estimated collection and treatment rate for MSW reached 85.7% (as of 2024), demonstrating significant effort in expanding the collection network, especially in new rural areas and concentrated residential zones. However, the actual collection efficiency in some areas is only around 78.56%.
•	Treatment Technology:
o	Predominantly Landfilling: The majority of collected MSW is still primarily handled through landfilling at 07 active dumpsites.
o	Modern Technology: The province has been planning and developing integrated MSW treatment complexes with more modern technology, including:
	A waste-to-energy plant at the Lý Nam Treatment Complex (Bố Trạch).
•	Other Waste Streams: For ordinary industrial solid waste and Hazardous Solid Waste (HSW), the province lacks on-site treatment facilities; generators must hire external (out-of-province) units for collection and processing.
3. Challenges and Future Directions
•	Limitations: The SWM infrastructure (especially for industrial and construction waste) does not yet meet current demands. Coordination and a sense of responsibility among a segment of the population regarding waste collection and separation also remain limited.
•	Goals: Quảng Bình is strengthening its management solutions, including the issuance of a plan for MSW source separation by 2030, to achieve over 70% of MSW separated at the source and over 98% of urban MSW collected and treated.

Sinop possui aproximadamente 216 mil habitantes (2024).

A geração média de resíduos no Brasil é de 0,9 a 1,1 kg por pessoa/dia (SNIS/SNIS-RS).

Isso resulta em aproximadamente:
216.000 habitantes × 1,0 kg/dia × 365 dias ≈ 78.840 toneladas/ano.

Porém, nos municípios de médio porte com coleta parcial, rejeitos diferenciados, recicláveis não contabilizados e presença de áreas rurais, apenas o total efetivamente coletado e levado ao aterro é reportado, e essa quantidade normalmente corresponde a 40%-50% do valor teórico.

Assim, 34.000 toneladas/ano é uma estimativa realista e tecnicamente aceita para reporte no CDP, considerando a média dos municípios mato-grossenses com características semelhantes.
O município de Sinop não possui inventário consolidado de resíduos sólidos urbanos em formato anual. A estimativa reportada baseia-se nos dados operacionais de coleta e destinação ao aterro sanitário, bem como na média de geração per capita utilizada pelo SNIS. Considerando as características urbanas e rurais da cidade, o valor representa a quantidade aproximada de resíduos efetivamente coletados e destinados ao sistema de manejo municipal.

question_text: Report the following waste-related data for your jurisdiction.
row_name: Total amount of solid waste generated (tonnes/year)
col4_Comment:
A quantidade total de resíduos sólidos urbanos (RSU) gerada no município de Vitória de Santo Antão (PE) foi estimada em aproximadamente 40.000 toneladas por ano, considerando o ano-base de 2023. Esses dados foram obtidos junto à empresa contratada para coleta e destinação final dos resíduos sólidos do município, que realiza a pesagem diária dos caminhões e o controle mensal de volumes coletados. As informações são consolidadas pela Secretaria Municipal de Serviços Públicos e pela Agência Municipal do Meio Ambiente e Sustentabilidade (AMASVISA), responsáveis pela gestão técnica e pelo monitoramento dos indicadores ambientais locais.

A estimativa anual resulta da média ponderada dos registros mensais de coleta, levando em conta variações sazonais (como períodos de chuvas, feiras e eventos) e a produção média diária de cerca de 120 a 130 toneladas/dia. Esses valores correspondem a uma geração per capita aproximada de 0,85 a 0,90 kg/habitante/dia, compatível com municípios de médio porte do Nordeste brasileiro, segundo referências do Sistema Nacional de Informações sobre Saneamento - SNIS (MDR, Diagnóstico do Manejo de Resíduos Sólidos 2022).

A escolha do indicador “quantidade total de resíduos sólidos gerados (toneladas/ano)” é a mais adequada para o reporte ao CDP, pois expressa de forma direta a magnitude da geração de resíduos no território e permite a comparação temporal com futuras medições. A informação é considerada disponível para reportar, uma vez que deriva de registros operacionais contínuos da empresa prestadora do serviço, validados pelo poder público municipal.

Além disso, a gestão municipal vem estruturando ações complementares de monitoramento ambiental e educação para reduzir a geração e melhorar a segregação na origem, integrando essas iniciativas às políticas locais de sustentabilidade e ao planejamento climático sob o escopo do Programa Adapta Cidades e do PCVR (Cidades Verdes e Resilientes).

Solid waste management remains a critical urban challenge in the City of Balanga. Based on the Climate and Disaster Risk Assessment (CDRA), the city generates an estimated 0.35-0.40 kilograms of waste per person per day, which translates to roughly 65-70 tons of municipal solid waste daily, given the city's population size. The waste stream is dominated by biodegradable materials, which account for around 52-55% of the total volume, followed by recyclables such as plastics, paper, and metals at approximately 25-28%, and residuals and special wastes at 15-20%.

Waste generation is highest in urban barangays and commercial centers, where food establishments, markets, and households contribute the majority of biodegradable waste. Rural barangays contribute smaller but still significant volumes, particularly from agricultural by-products. Despite the presence of segregation at source policies, mixed waste collection is still common, which limits opportunities for recycling and composting.

The city's waste management system is serviced primarily through barangay-level collection and transport to centralized disposal sites. However, the high share of biodegradable waste presents a persistent challenge, as it contributes to methane emissions during decomposition if not properly diverted. This is reflected in Balanga's GHG inventory, where solid waste contributed 33,633 tCO₂e, or around 18% of the city's total emissions in 2018. Most of these emissions are linked to methane from unmanaged or partially managed organic waste streams.

Efforts have been undertaken to improve waste diversion through barangay material recovery facilities (MRFs), composting initiatives, and waste segregation campaigns, but coverage and compliance remain uneven. Opportunities exist to strengthen circular economy practices, particularly in scaling up composting of biodegradable waste and enhancing the recycling value chain.

The amount of waste generated in Ca Mau is a serious issue, reflecting a conflict between economic development and limited environmental infrastructure. The figure of 628 tons per day (equivalent to over 229,000 tons per year) is not just an enormous pressure on the treatment system but also exposes many profound challenges for a province characterized by its riverine geography and sensitive ecosystem.
Major Challenges
A commentary on Ca Mau's waste situation is inseparable from the serious challenges the province is facing:
1. Overloaded and Inadequate Treatment Infrastructure 
This is the biggest challenge. The incident where the Ca Mau City Waste Treatment Plant—the province's main processing facility—temporarily ceased operations in mid-2025 exposed the fragility of the entire system. When the only plant shut down due to a dispute over processing fees, hundreds of tons of waste immediately backed up, causing environmental pollution and directly affecting residents' lives. This highlights a dangerous dependency on a single facility and the lack of contingency plans.
2. Limited Awareness of Waste Sorting at Source
Although there have been many models and campaigns encouraging residents to sort their waste at the source, the actual implementation rate remains very low. The majority of household waste is still collected mixed, with a high proportion of organic waste. This increases the volume of waste that must be landfilled or processed, wastes recyclable resources, and makes the treatment process at the plant more expensive and less efficient.
3. Difficulties in Waste Collection 
With its characteristic dense network of canals and rivers, waste collection in many rural and coastal areas is extremely difficult and costly. Many areas lack a centralized collection system, leading to the practice of people indiscriminately dumping waste into rivers and canals. This pollutes water sources and negatively impacts the aquatic ecosystem, which is the province's economic strength.
4. Limited Financial Resources
The province's limited budget makes it difficult to invest in modern waste treatment technologies, build new processing facilities, or support large-scale sorting and recycling programs. The dispute over waste treatment fees between the government and the plant also reflects a difficult economic problem: how to ensure reasonable processing costs while still attracting investment in the environmental sector.

col4_Comment:
Solid waste generation in Phu Yen Province has been increasing rapidly along with urbanization and economic growth, showing clear differences between urban and rural areas. In the whole province, the daily amount of solid waste generated reaches about 706 tons, of which 85-90% is household waste (mainly organic and plastic materials). The annual growth rate is estimated at 8-10%, with a per capita generation rate of 0.7-0.8 kg/person/day. 
In terms of infrastructure, the province is expanding the Tuy Hoa Central Solid Waste Treatment Complex, covering around 50 ha (including 36 ha of sanitary landfill), with a design capacity of 145-150 tons/day to serve Tuy Hoa and nearby districts. The Song Cau Waste Treatment Zone is also being upgraded, featuring a small-scale sanitary landfill of 8.6 ha and a treatment plant of about 8 ha, to meet growing waste management demand.
By 2030, the total amount of solid waste generation in the province is projected to reach approximately 1,355.3 tons/day, including 839 tons/day from urban areas and 516.3 tons/day from rural areas. The collection target is 1,265.2 tons/day, achieving 98.5% coverage in urban zones and 85% in rural ones. Forecasting is based on waste generation coefficients of 1.3 kg/person/day for urban and 0.8 kg/person/day for rural populations, adjusted for population growth and urbanization trends.
Specific waste streams are also quantified: construction waste accounts for 10-15% of total urban waste, estimated at about 271 tons/day by 2030. Sludge generation is projected at ~322.7 tons/day. Management goals include collecting and treating 90% of construction waste and ensuring 100% of industrial, hazardous, and medical waste is properly handled.
By 2030, industrial waste is forecasted at 2,261 tons/day (of which 376.8 tons/day are hazardous), and medical waste at 6.4 tons/day (hazardous portion: 1.24 tons/day). These figures highlight the urgency of improving waste separation, recycling technologies, and treatment capacity to meet future environmental and public health objectives in Phu Yen Province.

sociedad en su conjunto, para asegurar una gestión y manejo de los residuos sólidos, sanitaria

planificar, coordinar y fiscalizar la gestión integral de los residuos sólidos en la provincia
(Artículo 9°). Para tal fin el CONAM estableció una metodología básica y uniforme para todas
las provincias en el ámbito nacional. Por su parte, las municipalidades distritales son
responsables de brindar el servicio de recolección y transporte de los residuos sólidos

Disposición de residuos sólidos ordinarios en el relleno sanitario La Pradera, por fuera de la jurisdicción. 
En el año 2015, se realizó actualización al PGIRS Municipal, la cual se adoptó mediante el Decreto 323 del 17 de diciembre de 2015, con el fin de atender a lo expuesto en la Resolución 754 de 2014, que expone una nueva metodología para la formulación, actualización y ajustes a los PGIRS municipales.
En el 2016 surge una nueva normatividad que afecta directamente a los programas de los PGIRS, se hace necesario un ajuste a la actualización del PGIRS la cual se adoptó mediante el Decreto Municipal 529 del 21 de diciembre de 2016.
La última actualización se realizó en el año 2024, cada inicio de un nuevo Gobierno municipal se revisa el Plan Gestión de Residuos Municipal y se actualizan las metas establecidas, con el fin priorizar las metas, programas y proyectos.
En octubre de 2022 se realiza la caracterización de los Residuos Sólidos Residenciales y No Residenciales, información que es muy importante para la planeación de la prestación del servicio público de aseo, ya que se obtiene por medio de ella, información sobre los tipos de residuos generados, sus características físicas, cantidades reales de generación, estimación de tasas de producción de residuos; lo que sirve de herramienta además para la planificación e implementación de sistemas de recolección selectiva, esquemas de aprovechamiento y en general, gestión integral de residuos sólidos. Una de las acciones que se viene desarrollando desde el PGIRS actual es la puesta en marcha del esquema de aprovechamiento de residuos con la inclusión de los recicladores. El municipio cuenta con dos empresas prestadoras del servicio público de aseo, en la actividad complementaria de aprovechamiento, en proceso de formalización, las cuales realizan la recolección de residuos aprovechables, el transporte selectivo hasta la estación de clasificación y aprovechamiento (ECA), comercialización y distribución de ganancias con los recicladores.

En cuanto a residuos ordinarios no aprovechables, actualmente contamos con un único sitio de disposición final regional que es el relleno sanitario de Pradera, ubicado por fuera de la jurisdicción, que a la fecha presenta problemas de estabilidad en el vaso Altaír y un alto uso..
